_note: Job A batch 6. Past-due claims due 2026-04-04 to 2026-07-04. Several of these are read-aloud news items the extractor already marked n/a; they are recorded as unfalsifiable with the underlying facts attached rather than left in the queue.

evidence.summary: NASA held a Moon Base event at headquarters on 26 May 2026 at which administrator Jared Isaacman announced three lunar missions targeted for launch by the end of 2026 and a Phase One programme of up to 25 missions and 21 landings through 2029, saying America is returning to the moon to stay.
evidence.rationale: A moon base did become public discussion, and the announcement was the biggest lunar programme news of the year. The date fails: he put the space race on 4 April and the announcement came on 26 May, seven weeks later. The base rate also cuts deep. Artemis has been a funded programme with a stated surface-base objective since 2019, Isaacman's appointment and lunar priorities were public through 2025, and a Chinese 2030 crewed target has kept space-race framing in the press continuously.

evidence.summary: On Easter Sunday, 5 April 2026, gunmen attacked two worship services in Ariko, Kachia County, Kaduna state, Nigeria, killing 12 Christians and kidnapping dozens, days after 17 were killed in Benue state. The same day in Gujranwala, Pakistan, a truck was driven into an Easter sunrise procession of more than 200 worshippers, injuring about 60. No attack occurred on an American church or Easter egg hunt.
evidence.rationale: He flagged it on 19 February as new material to take note of, and on 23 March added Africa highlighted, and Easter services were attacked, in Africa. That is closer than most items here. Two deductions, both large. Nigeria is the deadliest country in the world for Christians, with attacks on churches at Easter in most recent years, so an Easter attack there is close to the base rate rather than a departure from it. And the American half, which is what he was actually praying over, produced nothing. His detail about attacks on the Muslim side also does not match: the victims were Christians.

evidence.summary: A Deuteronomy 28 blessing spoken over the second week of April 2026 for an unnamed audience. No outcome is stated or measurable.
evidence.rationale: The extractor flagged it before the fact and correctly: a blessing spoken over a week has no threshold and no subject. Recorded to clear it from the queue.

evidence.summary: The president was engaged through the Easter period in the Iran war that began 28 February 2026 and the ceasefire announced 8 April 2026. No episode was reported that could be characterised as a distinct period of visible confusion.
evidence.rationale: Appearing confused is a judgment about a person's demeanour with no threshold, and it is one every political opponent asserts continuously. There is no observation that could have falsified it. Worth noting the structure: the prayer attached, that he take no counsel even from those he thinks he can trust, means any decision he takes can be read either as the confusion or as the answer.

evidence.summary: Yom HaShoah fell on 13-14 April 2026 and was marked in Israel and internationally in the usual way. No notable incident occurred on that date.
evidence.rationale: A date named nearly five months ahead with instruction to pray over it and nothing attached to it, and the date passed unremarkably. He says himself that he does not understand it and it does not matter, it is to be prayed out, which is honest and also removes any content. Scored as expired rather than unfalsifiable because a specific date was given and a specific date can be checked.

evidence.summary: Ukrainian long-range strikes on Russian oil refineries and Black Sea export infrastructure continued through April 2026 on the dates he lists, and reports circulated of oil falling as rain near struck facilities.
evidence.rationale: All three tellings are news read aloud after the events, and the extractor marked each n/a at the time. There is no forward claim to score. Recorded with the underlying facts so the row is closed and so the pattern is countable: a growing share of the recent corpus consists of dated news items assembled into a pattern after the fact.

evidence.summary: The 2026 Boston Marathon was run on 20 April 2026 without incident, John Korir setting a course record of 2:01:52. No significant violent event occurred in the United States between 19 April and 1 May 2026.
evidence.rationale: A thirteen-day window, a named event inside it and an explicit expectation of violence, and nothing happened. The supporting argument is retrospective by construction: Oklahoma City, Columbine and Lexington are three dates assembled after the fact from a calendar that has 365 of them, which the extractor marked n/a. Naming the window in advance is what makes it scoreable, and it failed.

evidence.summary: April 2026 brought twin X2.5 solar flares from one active region on 24 April and an M6 flare on 26 April, with a coronal mass ejection giving Earth a glancing blow on 26 April that produced only minor high-latitude aurora. No unusual meteor activity or atmospheric phenomena were reported for the month.
evidence.rationale: There was notable solar activity in the month he named, said five days ahead of it. The base rate takes nearly all of it: the sun is close to solar maximum, X-class flares occurred in most months of 2025 and 2026, and signs in the heavens with no threshold is satisfied by any flare, aurora or bright meteor. The specific detail he added, meteors and lights coming into the atmosphere, has no match. He also confirms the mechanism in the telling itself: somebody sent it to Braden who found it.

evidence.summary: April 2026 contained the Iran war ceasefire announced on 8 April, continued Ukrainian strikes on Russian refineries, and Easter attacks in Nigeria and Pakistan. The claim attaches no event to the month.
evidence.rationale: The content is typography: April seen large, its capital A emboldened and outlined in black with something like a slide on the side. No event, no domain, no direction. Any April would satisfy it. This is the purest example in the database of a month named with nothing in it, and it is recorded so the category can be counted rather than argued about.

evidence.summary: No revival or religious outpouring beginning in Argentina was reported in April 2026, and no start of a wealth transfer is identifiable.
evidence.rationale: A named country and a named month, which makes it scoreable, and nothing was reported. Argentina has a real revival history that would make such an event newsworthy and findable if it had occurred. Scored as a miss rather than unfalsifiable because the specificity was his own.

evidence.summary: The claim concerns one unidentified individual's gout resolving within three days. Untreated acute gout attacks typically resolve within one to two weeks, and treated attacks often improve within a few days.
evidence.rationale: The person is unnamed, so no outcome can be observed, and he says in the telling that it may not be for everybody but for one person in particular, which makes the claim unlocatable by design. The clinical base rate is worth recording anyway: gout attacks improving within days is the normal course with treatment.

evidence.summary: The National Day of Prayer was observed on 7 May 2026. No outpouring or unusual event was reported at it.
evidence.rationale: A Holy Ghost sound of a mighty rushing wind has no observable threshold, and the claim is explicitly conditioned on the 2 Chronicles humbling, which supplies the reason for any absence. The extractor flagged the companion telling on the same grounds. Recorded to close the row.

evidence.summary: Trump announced on 8 May 2026 that Russia and Ukraine had agreed to a three-day ceasefire for Victory Day, running 9 to 11 May, with 1,000 prisoners released by each side. Zelenskyy and Ushakov both confirmed it.
evidence.rationale: The telling is dated 12 May, four days after the announcement, and consists of him being told the date and reading the report. The only forward element is that he says he saw four, matched afterwards to a three-day ceasefire announced on the 8th, which is a number attached to an event after the event. The extractor marked it a real dated announcement matched to a number, which is the right description. Nothing here could have failed.

evidence.summary: Nothing of note occurred on or around 10 May 2026 in the crypto context under discussion. The date is arrived at in conversation as a guess.
evidence.rationale: He says maybe May 10th or something like that, some time in May. That is a guess offered as a guess, with no event attached, and it is recorded as such rather than counted either way. Worth keeping beside the dated claims because it shows how loosely some dates enter the material.

evidence.summary: Trump announced at the National Prayer Breakfast on 5 February 2026 that an event on the National Mall on 17 May 2026, titled Rededicate 250 and billed as a National Jubilee of Prayer, Praise and Thanksgiving, would rededicate the United States as one nation under God. A 29 January 2026 proclamation had already declared 2026 a Year of Celebration and Rededication.
evidence.rationale: The event happened on the day he named. He named it on 12 May, three months after it had been publicly announced from the National Prayer Breakfast and covered widely in religious media, which is his own audience. There is no forward content: this is a diary entry. Recorded as partial because the statement is accurate, and the rationale is the reason it means nothing.

evidence.summary: Pentecost Sunday 2026 fell on 24 May, a fixed date on the Western church calendar computed from Easter.
evidence.rationale: They work out a date from the church calendar for something they intend to hold. The extractor recorded that it is read off the calendar rather than seen, and that is the whole of it.

evidence.summary: The claim concerns an unidentified listener's child due in May 2026, said to be a girl. No outcome is recorded. Roughly 51 percent of US births are male.
evidence.rationale: The extractor noted the sex is a fifty fifty call that could be checked, and that is right in principle and impossible in practice, because the listener is not identified anywhere in the corpus. Recorded as unfalsifiable with the base rate stated, so that if the person is ever identified the row can be reopened.

evidence.summary: Maduro was captured in a US military operation on 3 January 2026 and taken to the United States, with at least 32 Cuban soldiers killed. Cuba saw sustained protest through 2026, with the Cuban Conflict Observatory recording 953 demonstrations in January, 1,245 in March, 1,133 in April and 1,311 in May. No regime change occurred in Cuba, and analysts describe no plausible quick transition in 2026. No American military action took place in Cuba.
evidence.rationale: The claim names 2027 and 2027 has not arrived, so a verdict now would be premature; evidence is recorded instead. What can be said: the March 2026 telling about American troops liberating Cuba in the days ahead has not happened, and the Venezuela half of the same telling had already happened when he said it, Maduro having been captured two months earlier. Cuba is genuinely more unstable than a year ago, which is the part a 2027 scorer should weigh against the base rate of a regime that has outlasted every previous prediction of its fall.

evidence.summary: A declaration over 2026 and over listeners' households, marriages and children, with no threshold given.
evidence.rationale: All three tellings were flagged unfalsifiable at extraction, and the second flag names the mechanism exactly: any large audience supplies both outcomes. This is the 2026 instance of the annual year-word, and it is scored the same way as open-door-2025 and soar-2024 so the pattern stays comparable across years.

evidence.summary: Jerome Powell's term as Federal Reserve chair ended in May 2026; the Board named him chair pro tempore on 15 May and Kevin Warsh was sworn in on 22 May 2026. Powell remains a Board governor with a term running to 2028.
evidence.rationale: A post did end in May, and his 13 May telling makes clear he means Powell. What removes almost all the value is that Powell's term end had been fixed and published since 2022, so a job ending in May 2026 was a calendar fact available to anyone. The passage also does not name the person, which is why it is scored separately from powell-out-in-january, where he did name him and put it in the wrong month.

evidence.summary: On 20 February 2026 the Supreme Court struck down the IEEPA reciprocal tariffs 6-3. The administration responded the same day with a 10 percent temporary import surcharge under Section 122 effective 24 February for 150 days, and announced a shift to Sections 232 and 301. The EU delayed ratification of US trade agreements and the legal basis of many bilateral deals was called into question.
evidence.rationale: A genuine global trade realignment around tariffs did land inside the window, and he named the mechanism, tariffs, and the horizon, clear into May 2026, back in July 2025. Held at partial because the realignment arrived three months early and by a route he never mentions, a Supreme Court ruling against the tariffs rather than their extension, and because tariffs were the single most discussed economic story of the period when he spoke, four months into the trade war.

evidence.summary: May 2026 included the Senate confirmation and swearing-in of a new Federal Reserve chair, a three-day Russia-Ukraine ceasefire announced on 8 May, and the National Jubilee of Prayer on 17 May.
evidence.rationale: Said on 1 May, the first day of the month, with no content beyond that the month is pivotal and important to remember. Every month contains events of consequence. There is no version of May that could have refuted this, and it belongs with the other named-month-with-nothing-in-it claims.

evidence.summary: The Air Force said on 2 May 2026 that the Qatari-donated Boeing 747-8 would be ready to serve as Air Force One that summer, and Trump unveiled the converted aircraft on 19 June 2026. The gift, valued around 400 million dollars, had been public since May 2025 and serves as a bridge aircraft until new Boeing planes arrive in 2028.
evidence.rationale: A new painted aircraft did arrive and the May timing matches the Air Force's readiness announcement, with the unveiling six weeks later. The distinguishing detail is wrong in the opposite direction: he said it would no longer be a great big plane but a fast one, and the aircraft is a 747-8, larger than the 757 it replaces in his framing. The whole thing had also been in the news for a year when he described it in April 2026.

evidence.summary: US measles cases in the first seven months of 2026 exceeded all of 2025, itself the worst year in three decades, reaching 2,777 confirmed cases by 20 August 2026 across 36 outbreaks, with kindergarten vaccination coverage down to 92.4 percent. Measles in the United States is seasonal with a late-winter to spring peak. H5N1 remained established in dairy herds without sustained human transmission.
evidence.rationale: Seven tellings and a real outbreak that does broadly follow the shape he drew: rising from autumn, heaviest late winter through spring, easing over summer. That shape is also the ordinary seasonality of measles and of respiratory disease generally, which is the whole difficulty. And the extractor put the decisive objection in the falsifier before any outcome was known: the Lord took the calendar and counted it backwards, which makes the sequence readable in either direction. A claim that can be read forwards or backwards cannot be scored above partial no matter what happens.

evidence.summary: No place, target or scale is named. FBI quarterly data through 2026 show robbery continuing the multi-year decline recorded since 2022.
evidence.rationale: One word, one month and no location. Robbery occurs continuously everywhere, so the claim is satisfied by definition and refuted by nothing. Recorded with the national trend for context, which happens to run the other way.

evidence.summary: No Chinese military action against Taiwan occurred. Beijing continued coercive pressure short of blockade or invasion through 2026; US officials place Xi's capability deadline at 2027 and Pentagon assessments hold that a blockade would likely fail.
evidence.rationale: Three tellings across December 2025 to March 2026, each giving a duration of two or three days, one of them explicitly not three days from now, and no move was made in the window. The claim is unusually specific for this corpus, naming a mechanism, a duration and novel weapons, and that specificity is exactly why it can be scored as a clean miss rather than left open.

evidence.summary: No fertiliser-truck bombing or comparable attack on the Oklahoma City model occurred in the United States between June 2025 and mid-2026, and no rail attack of the kind described took place. The largest disrupted domestic plot in the period, the December 2025 Turtle Island Liberation Front case, involved improvised explosive devices intended for commercial targets rather than a vehicle bomb.
evidence.rationale: Named method, named vehicles, named targets, repeated three times over four months, and it did not happen. This is among the more falsifiable warnings in the corpus and it failed cleanly, which is worth stating plainly beside the Butler warning that did land.

evidence.summary: No cluster of financial or housing developments distinguishable from the ordinary occurred in May 2026. Existing home sales continued the modest recovery begun in late 2025.
evidence.rationale: Many avenues opening at once so that it looks like open doors, over an unnamed audience, has no threshold. The one instruction with a referent, watch the housing market, is not a claim. Recorded to close the row.

evidence.summary: Japan's Financial Services Agency reclassified qualifying foreign trust-type stablecoins as electronic payment instruments under the Payment Services Act with effect from 1 June 2026, with the remaining Cabinet Office ordinances following on 13 June. USDC was expected to be among the first to qualify.
evidence.rationale: The extractor's note is right: a real dated policy change read out on air and offered as confirmation of the earlier crypto material. He is reading it on 20 May, after the rules were published, so nothing was foreseen. The fact is recorded because the row should carry it, not because there is a claim to score.

evidence.summary: Nothing notable occurred in the United States between 25 May and 4 June 2026. Memorial Day, 25 May 2026, and the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier ceremony proceeded normally.
evidence.rationale: An eleven-day window named eleven days ahead, with imagery attached but no event, and the window closed empty. The Tomb of the Unknown Soldier and flowers point at the Memorial Day ceremony, which happens every year on that date and happened this year. Scored as expired because the window was his own and was specific.

evidence.summary: The GENIUS Act of July 2025 created a federal framework for payment stablecoins, and crypto market-structure legislation continued through 2026, with Japan recognising foreign stablecoins from 1 June 2026. No single digital identity and payment system exists, and no move toward one has been enacted.
evidence.rationale: The regulatory settlement half is real: the sector did move from the wild west to a licensed framework over 2025 and 2026, and he described that in February 2025 before the GENIUS Act passed, though after the bill had been introduced and the administration had made stablecoin legislation an announced priority. The beast-system half is not scoreable and he says so himself in December 2025, putting the full manifestation with the antichrist, which places it permanently beyond checking.

evidence.summary: Global protest activity in 2025 exceeded the twelve months before the 2020 BLM protests in frequency, with more than 70 countries affected, Indonesian riots in August 2025 causing over 50 million dollars of insured losses and Nepalese protests over 200 million. Analysts state that no single 2025 or 2026 event has matched the roughly 3 billion dollars of insured losses from the 2020 US unrest, and US cities saw no rioting or looting on the 2020 scale.
evidence.rationale: The global half has support: measured protest frequency is above the pre-2020 baseline and risk analysts expected 2026 to be more disruptive still, and he said it in September 2025 before the largest of those waves. The specific comparison he made fails on the only quantified measure available: 2020 remains the larger event by insured loss, and the American cities he later named did not riot. His October claim to have called the Barcelona demonstrations is a fulfilment assertion made three days after them.

evidence.summary: No lone-wolf attack occurred in San Antonio in June 2026, and no attacker in a black hoodie was identified. No wave of lone-wolf attacks by sympathisers of a foreign cause occurred in the United States in the period.
evidence.rationale: The June 2026 telling is among the most specific in the whole corpus: a named city, a named month, one dominant attacker plus two others, a black hoodie, and his own reasoning for why it would stand out, that a hoodie in June in San Antonio is out of place. Nothing happened. Specificity is what makes a claim worth keeping, and this one earned a clean verdict.

evidence.summary: Gold rose through 4,500, 5,000 and 5,500 dollars an ounce into a January 2026 peak and silver reached a record 121.64 dollars on 29 January 2026, after which gold fell nearly 30 percent and silver roughly halved, before gold recovered to 4,633 dollars by 21 August 2026 and silver past 67 dollars. Central banks bought a record 288.9 tonnes in the second quarter of 2026.
evidence.rationale: The 7 November 2025 telling is the scoreable one and it is the best-formed market call in this database: a short-lived wave with gold on it, and the opportunity then visibly closing. Gold and silver ran hard into late January 2026 and then fell 30 and 50 percent, which is exactly a window that opened and shut. Held at partial for three reasons. The gold run was already two years old and at record highs when he said it. The 2023 telling in the same claim is unfalsifiable and the extractor said so. And the great storm he attached to the far side of the window has not arrived.

evidence.summary: Coachella 2026 ran 10 to 19 April 2026 at the Empire Polo Club without incident, and no attack occurred at a large US festival or gathering through the summer of 2026.
evidence.rationale: The content is a prayer over federal and local agencies doing their jobs, not a claim that anything will happen. Nothing did. Recorded as unfalsifiable rather than as a miss, because unlike the Chicago parade and Sugar Bowl warnings this one never asserts a threat.

evidence.summary: The ninety days from 13 November 2025 ended on 11 February 2026, before the Iran war began on 28 February 2026. The two-week conditional ceasefire in that war was announced on 8 April 2026. No single crisis ran continuously from November 2025 to 4 July 2026.
evidence.rationale: The arithmetic does not work and the passage shows it not working: he recounts someone else's ninety-day warning, is corrected to forty, settles back on ninety, and then says ninety days was also the timeframe he was given running all the way to the Fourth of July, which is 233 days rather than 90. A number that changes inside the sentence and does not reach the date it is said to reach cannot be scored as a match, and the window it does define closed before the year's major crisis began.
